They could come from the decay of two heavy KK gluons gkk(3.6TeV) and gkk(8.6TeV) into pairs of KK quarks qkk(1TeV) and qkk(2.1TeV). Present limits on gkk into top pairs seem to exclude gkk(3.6TeV) but these limits assume a dominant decay into top pairs, which can be questioned as was the case in our study of KK graviton decays. The cross section predicted for gkk(8.6) requires a BR into a pair of qkk(2.1TeV) or order 10% which is not unlikely. We also discuss the issue of a hierarchy between the KK graviton masses and the vector boson masses and the solution provided by the RS multi-brane models. Prospects for reaching a 6 s.d. level local evidence with RUN3 data are promising for 3 channels. KK excitations of the Z boson are discussed and appear also promising. Indirect evidences for these particles are also presented.

title: Probing the QCD critical point through linearized sound wave dispersion and attenuation at finite baryon density
abstract: We investigate the linearized sound-channel response of a finite baryon density Israel-Stewart hydrodynamic system coupled to a parameterized equation of state containing a critical end point. The attenuation of sound is characterized by a threshold wavelength below which sound perturbations are strongly damped. We systematically study the dependence of this threshold scale on the non-universal parameters of the Beam Energy Scan Theory (BEST) equation of state framework. In our present study, the threshold wavelength remains finite but develops a pronounced peak in the vicinity of the critical end point, indicating strong absorption of sound modes on fireball-scale wavelengths. We further estimate the impact of this enhanced attenuation on the linearized anisotropic flow response and find a reduction of the elliptic and triangular flow harmonics near the critical region. Our results establish a phenomenological connection between critical sound attenuation, Mach cone like correlations, and the linearized flow response in baryon rich QCD matter. These results suggest a non-monotonic beam-energy dependence of the sound attenuation scale. Together with a corresponding suppression of Mach cone like correlations and the linearized anisotropic flow response, they may provide a consistent signature that the system trajectory passes close to the critical point of the chosen equation of state.

title: The Future Circular Collider as a photon-photon collider
abstract: The CERN Future Circular Collider (FCC) offers a unique programme of photon-photon interactions in electron-positron, proton-proton, proton-lead, and lead-lead collisions, by exploiting the high-luminosity equivalent photon fluxes associated with the charged beams. Within the equivalent photon approximation, the electromagnetic fields of relativistic charged particles are described in terms of fluxes of quasireal photons. The complementary photon fluxes, energies, and virtualities available across the FCC operation modes provide access to a broad range of two-photon invariant masses and associated physics measurements. Physics opportunities open to study are highlighted, focusing on the exclusive production of C-even resonances, including the SM Higgs boson and searches for spin-0 axion-like (ALPs) and spin-2 graviton-like (GLPs) particles decaying back into photon pairs. These prospective studies demonstrate the potential to observe photon-fusion production of the Higgs boson for all colliding modes, as well as sensitivity to photon-coupled ALPs and GLPs with masses extending up to the kinematic reach of FCC-ee and into the multi-TeV range at FCC-hh collisions, with significant improvements over existing constraints.

title: On Quantised Magnetic Monopoles in the Nonlocal Electromagnetic Field
abstract: We consider Maxwell electrodynamics in the presence of both electric and magnetic charges when the fields are made nonlocal by the prescription of the Moffat-Thompson nonlocal quantum field theory. The symmetry between the electric and magnetic equations is preserved, while a point magnetic charge is a finite distribution and its field energy becomes finite. When Dirac's quantisation condition $eg=2πn$ is imposed, the magnetic self-energy is found to be much greater than the corresponding electric one. We conclude that magnetic monopoles may be permitted by the theory and yet require a very large energy for their production, thus making their abundance and detection a difficult feat.

title: Scalar and spin polarizabilities of singly heavy baryons within heavy baryon chiral perturbation theory
abstract: We present a systematic study of the scalar electromagnetic and spin polarizabilities of spin-1/2 singly charmed baryons at $\mathcal{O}(p^4)$ within the framework of heavy baryon chiral perturbation theory. Our results show that the higher-order corrections to the electric polarizability are small, while those to the magnetic polarizability are relatively larger due to the small mass splitting of singly charmed baryons and are closely related to transition magnetic moments. Furthermore, we find that the spin polarizabilities of singly charmed baryons, except for $γ_{M1M1}$, are much smaller than those of the nucleons. We have also calculated the polarizabilities for singly bottom baryons, with the results showing generally larger values than those of singly charmed baryons.

title: BPS vortex from nonpolynomial scalar QED in a $\mathbb{C}\mathrm{P}^1$-Maxwell theory
abstract: We investigate a generalized gauged $\mathbb{C}\mathrm{P}^1$-Maxwell theory in which the electromagnetic sector acquires a field-dependent magnetic permeability generated dynamically through fermionic vacuum polarization. We couple a Dirac fermion with an effective mass to a gauged $\mathbb{C}\mathrm{P}^1$ sigma model whose target space carries the Fubini-Study metric. Integrating out the Dirac fermion at one loop induces a logarithmic correction to the Maxwell kinetic term. This dependence is retained in the planar effective theory after dimensional reduction. Within this framework, one builds a generalized $\mathbb{C}\mathrm{P}^1$-Maxwell model by admitting Bogomol'nyi-Prasad-Sommerfield (BPS) configurations. Taking this into account, we solved the self-dual equations that describe vortex-like solutions with quantized magnetic flux.

title: Probing the QCD Conformal Window with Four-Quark Operators
abstract: The infrared fate of QCD-like theories and their conformal window for different numbers or flavours and colour remains an open question with applications ranging from high-energy to condensed-matter systems. A hallmark of phase transitions from a conformal to symmetry breaking phase can be the presence of classically irrelevant operators that provide relevant deformation in the infrared. We investigate this scenario by computing anomalous dimensions of all four-quark operators, with or without chiral symmetry, at four-loop order as well as the dimension-six gluonic operator at three loops in Veneziano QCD. Scaling dimensions are derived in a systematic conformal expansion. These results are improved with various resummation techniques and we estimate their uncertainties. We find no concrete evidence for a composite operator effectively describing a merger with the QCD fixed point.

title: Quark + diquark description of nucleon gravitational form factors
abstract: We present parameter-free predictions for the nucleon gravitational form factors (GFFs) using a Poincare-covariant quark+diquark Faddeev equation. We provide the full GFFs ($A$, $J$, $D$, and $\bar{c}$) along with their species decompositions into quark and gluon contributions. Based on the diquark breakdown, we find that while the scalar diquark component dominates the nucleon's energy, spin, and mechanical properties, the axial-vector component plays an indispensable role. The GFF $B(Q^2)$ is predicted to be vanishingly small but nonvanishing at finite $Q^2$; its physical origin is deeply rooted in the nucleon' s internal structure through cancellations in both the diquark content and the $u/d$ flavor sectors. Furthermore, our results for $\bar{c}(Q^2)$ confirm the fundamental symmetry requirements of the approach. Compared with lQCD, our calculated $D$-term and various spatial radii are somewhat smaller in magnitude. This systematic underestimation is primarily driven by the gluon sector and can be attributed to the omission of meson cloud effects, suggesting that these effects impact the gluon distribution more significantly than the quark distribution. Finally, our analysis of the energy density based on two extrapolation schemes reveals that the presence of a negative central energy density is highly model-dependent.

title: General Formulation of Covariant Tensor Amplitudes for Purely Hadronic and Single-photon Radiative Cascade Decays
abstract: We present a unified method for generating Lorentz-covariant partial-wave amplitudes for multi-body purely hadronic and single-photon radiative cascade decays within the covariant $L$-$S$ tensor formalism. Based on the structural decoupling of external polarization wave functions, complex coupling parameters, and the core covariant amplitude tensor $U$, we establish a hierarchical vertex contraction procedure that explicitly incorporates intermediate-state cascade bridge projection operators $P^{(J_i)}(p_i)$ and parent-frame definite-spin projection operators $P^{(S_{BC})}(p_A)$. This rigorous treatment guarantees the Rarita-Schwinger symmetry, tracelessness, and transversality conditions across different reference frames, fundamentally eliminating the unphysical longitudinal and trace contaminations induced by Lorentz boosts in cascade decays. Furthermore, we formulate a general covariant tensor representation for single-photon radiative decays $A(J_M) \to γ+ X(J_X)$ that strictly satisfies photon gauge invariance ($q^λV_{\dotsλ\dots} = 0$) in the Lorenz gauge. Built upon normal- and anomalous-parity fundamental transverse tensors ($K_{μν}$ and $S_{μν}$), universal recursive formulas are derived via the systematic replacement $g_{μν} \to q_μp_{Aν}$, accompanied by exact rules for matching the orbital angular momentum ranks of Blatt-Weisskopf centrifugal barrier factors $B_{L_{\text{rad}}}$ and a spectator index pass-through mechanism for the photon polarization index.

title: Inclusive Heavy Quarkonium Production in Lepton-Hadron Scattering in a Joint QCD+QED Factorization Approach
abstract: The Electron-Ion Collider (EIC) will provide an opportunity for precision studies of heavy quarkonium production in electron-proton ($ep$) and electron-nucleus ($eA$) collisions. Comparing production in $ep$ and $eA$ collisions provides a clean, well-controlled experimental environment to study interactions between a heavy quark pair and nuclear matter and the formation of quarkonia in a nuclear medium. In this talk, we present the first calculation of heavy quarkonium production in both $ep$ and $eA$ collisions at EIC energies using a joint QCD+QED factorization framework that treats collision-induced QCD and QED radiation on equal footing, and discuss the role of the nuclear medium in exploring how a physical quarkonium is emerged from a produced heavy quark pair. We also systematically extend our calculation to include next-to-leading power contributions in the inverse power expansion of quarkonium transverse momentum, and discuss the matching of our calculations to fixed-order calculations in the nonrelativistic Quantum Chromodynamics (NRQCD) approach.

title: A dual-moment phenomenological framework for gravitational,electromagnetic and strong interactions
abstract: The unification of fundamental interactions remains an outstanding open problem in fundamental physics. Most existing unification schemes rely on extra dimensions, exotic symmetries, or unobserved dynamical degrees of freedom. Here we construct a minimal classical phenomenological framework built on primitive charges and motion-induced kinetic dual moments. Gravitational, electromagnetic, and strong interactions are coherently formulated within a unified inverse-square-law structure. We postulate a universal coupling relation connecting source-charge couplings and moment-mediated couplings across these interaction sectors. Although weak-charge degrees of freedom can be formally accommodated within the formalism, full quantitative treatment of weak-interaction dynamics is left for future work. The model recovers well-established low-energy limits for planetary orbits, atomic systems, and heavy-quark hadrons. Importantly, it yields distinguishable corrections to light deflection by rapidly spinning compact objects, and three independent experimental schemes are proposed to test these predictions.

title: Symmetry-based resolution of pseudogauge ambiguities in local equilibrium
abstract: The total angular momentum current can be decomposed into orbital and spin contributions in different ways, known as pseudogauges. This freedom leads to ambiguities in the definition of local-equilibrium density operators, which in turn affect estimates of spin polarization in heavy-ion collisions. In this work, the pseudogauge ambiguity, together with other ambiguities associated with improvements of conserved currents, is reformulated in terms of spurious symmetries corresponding to conserved currents with vanishing total charge. A prescription for the unambiguous definition of a local-equilibrium density operator, defined as deviating from global equilibrium only by small gradients, is introduced using the currents associated with genuine symmetries. The resulting density operator is invariant under transformations that add improvement terms to local currents, including the energy-momentum tensor.

title: Longitudinal Parton Correlations in MRW-Type Unintegrated Double Parton Distributions
abstract: Double parton scattering offers a way to investigate correlations between partons inside the proton that are absent from the usual product approximation for double parton distributions. In this contribution, we discuss how these correlations enter unintegrated double parton distributions when transverse momentum is generated using MRW-type prescriptions. Starting from non-factorized GS09 distributions evolved to unequal scales, we examine the double LO-MRW, virtuality-ordered MRW, and modified KMRW constructions, focusing on their transverse-momentum dependence and flavor structure.

title: Quantum Field Approach to Relativistic Turbulence
abstract: The goal of this work is to apply quantum field theory methods to a typical relativistic hydrodynamic model. We shall take as representative model an Israel-Stewart framework, where the energy-momentum conservation laws for a conformal invariant fluid are supplemented by a Cattaneo-Maxwell equation for its viscous energy-momentum tensor. In these models the viscous energy-momentum tensor relaxes to its Landau-Lifshitz value on a finite time scale. We assume the parameters of the model depend on the speed of light $c$ in such a way that as $c\to\infty$ the fluid becomes an incompressible fluid obeying the Navier-Stokes equations. We show that because the relativistic model must be hyperbolic, each mode behaves as an overdamped oscillator with two decay constants, one of which diverges as $c\to\infty$. Thus for finite $c$ there are two basic patterns, one which contains only slowly decaying modes, and reproduces Kolmogorov turbulence when $c\to\infty$, and another made of fast decaying modes only. Each flow pattern is associated to definite relations among the velocity and viscous energy tensor correlators.

title: Quark-mass dependence of two-nucleon scattering
abstract: Understanding how the properties of the visible Universe depend on the parameters of the Standard Model of particle physics requires \emph{ab initio} theoretical computations. To that end, we investigate the quark-mass dependence of low-energy nucleon-nucleon scattering in the deuteron and dineutron channels. We perform lattice-QCD calculations at pion masses $M_π\approx 200$ and $280$ MeV and compare their results to phenomenology at the physical point and to a previous calculation at $M_π\approx 710$ MeV. Scattering amplitudes, phase shifts, and threshold parameters are determined from finite-volume spectra using quantization conditions that explicitly incorporate long-distance effects from one-pion exchange. We analyze the pion-mass dependence of scattering lengths and effective ranges using chiral effective field theory with Weinberg and Kaplan-Savage-Wise power countings. From this, we estimate the pion-mass derivatives of the inverse scattering lengths and binding momentum, at the physical point. Both power countings indicate that the deuteron unbinds near $M_π\approx 220$ MeV.

title: Colours and Flavours: ropes and colour reconnection as string multiplets
abstract: The increase of strange-hadron yields with event activity and the enhanced charm-baryon fractions in hadronic collisions motivate a microscopic examination of how the colour environment affects hadronization. We review and develop the string description of these effects, starting from the Lund fragmentation baseline in electron--positron annihilation and following colour correlations beyond the leading-colour approximation. Few-parton examples show how junction formation and rope hadronization arise from the same SU(3) colour structure, connecting baryon formation and the screening forces that govern strange-quark production. For nuclear collisions, we introduce a local escape criterion and a phenomenological saturation of the breakup force, motivated by a three-string example of screening through background colour correlations. With common settings, the combined prescription gives a satisfactory description of light-flavour ratios in pp and p--Pb and provides O--O predictions. Charm ratios reveal a substantial remaining deficit in $Ξ_c$ production, motivating separate tests of the fragmentation baseline and its extrapolation with activity.

title: Effects of Parton Pair Correlations on Direct-Photon Yields and Elliptic Flow in Heavy-Ion Collisions
abstract: Direct photons escape heavy-ion collisions with little rescattering, carrying information from the full emission history. Yet describing the measured direct-photon yield and the sizable elliptic flow $v_2$ together remains a long-standing challenge. Here we explore how correlations between emitting partons may affect both observables. The local $2\to2$ photon rate depends on the joint distribution of incoming partons, so a connected correlation between them can change photon emission without changing the one-particle distribution of medium particles. Once folded over the evolving medium in Au+Au and Pb+Pb collisions, the correlation raises the photon yield toward the fitted PHENIX and ALICE data and increases $v_2$ mainly at intermediate $p_T$. The fitted temperature dependence accounts for most of the net flow increase in this region, suggesting that the correlation changes the relative contributions between hotter and cooler regions.

title: Fate of chiral and $U(1)_A$ symmetries in hot QCD matter under background magnetic fields
abstract: We summarize our recent lattice QCD study of chiral and singlet $U(1)_A$ symmetry breaking in background magnetic fields. The magnetic field explicitly reduces the non-singlet flavor symmetry through the unequal light-quark electric charges. We therefore study two neutral-channel susceptibility differences: $χ_{π^0}-χ_σ$ for chiral symmetry breaking and $χ_{π^0}-χ_{δ^0}$ for singlet $U(1)_A$ symmetry breaking. The calculation uses fixed-scale $(2+1)$-flavor HISQ ensembles with $m_l=m_s^{\mathrm{phys}}/10$, corresponding to a zero-field pion mass of $M_π\simeq220\,\mathrm{MeV}$. Magnetic fields enhance both susceptibility differences at low temperatures. Near the crossover, sufficiently strong fields instead suppress both differences. The suppression sets in at larger magnetic fields and is milder for the singlet-axial susceptibility difference than for the neutral chiral susceptibility difference.

title: Phenomenology of genuine twist-three distributions from a global QCD analysis
abstract: We present an extraction and phenomenological study of genuine twist-three parton distribution functions (PDFs) through a global QCD analysis of the structure function $g_2$ in deep-inelastic scattering (DIS), its moment $d_2$, and single-/double-spin asymmetries in semi-inclusive DIS (SIDIS). The unified description of these processes clearly confirms the universality of genuine twist-three PDFs and the validity of QCD factorization theorems at this subleading level. The extraction is accompanied by several validation tests, tests of sum rules, comparisons with earlier literature, computation forces and average transverse momentum of partons. As a by-product, we also obtain Sivers and worm-gear-T transverse momentum dependent (TMD) distributions, which allows us to construct a tomographic picture of the proton based on substantially broader data.

title: Skyrmions coupled to the sigma meson
abstract: We propose a geometric coupling of the Skyrme model of nuclei to the scalar--isoscalar sigma meson by identifying the sigma field with the radial length of the chiral four-vector while preserving the topological protection of the baryon number. Restricting to the $B=1$ hedgehog ansatz, an asymptotic analysis of the field equations shows that the in-vacuum sigma mass $m_σ$ is replaced inside the nucleon by an effective in-medium mass $m_{σ,{\rm eff}} = 2m_π$. Full numerical integration via a double-shooting method and parameter optimization demonstrate that including the sigma meson leads to a remarkable improvement in the description of nucleon observables and to a pion decay constant very close to its physical value.

title: Hamiltonian Truncation Framework for Gauge Theories on the Interval
abstract: In this work, we investigate gauge theories in two dimensions nonperturbatively using the Hamiltonian truncation approach. Working on a spatial interval and adopting the axial gauge, we remove all gauge field degrees of freedom and express the interacting Hamiltonian in the eigenbasis of the free Dirac theory, truncated at a finite energy. As a benchmark we analyse the Schwinger model, where our numerical spectra agree closely with the exact results from bosonization across a wide range of couplings, validating the construction of the Hamiltonian. We then generalize the formulation to nonabelian gauge groups and apply it to SU(3) gauge theory with a single massless Dirac fermion. These results demonstrate that gauge theories can be explored nonperturbatively using a truncated Hamiltonian that generates evolutions in ordinary time, offering a complementary alternative to lattice field theory.

title: Form-Factor-Constrained Non-Factorized Transition-GPD Tomography of $N\toΔ(1232)$ Multipole Structure
abstract: A form-factor-constrained non-factorized transition-GPD reconstruction is developed for the $N\toΔ(1232)$ electromagnetic transition. The production input consists of the published CLAS magnetic multipole amplitude and electric and scalar/Coulomb quadrupole ratios. Additional external low-$Q^2$ ratio data are retained only as a separate ratio-sector diagnostic. The electroproduction quantities are propagated replica by replica and converted to the dimensionless Jones--Scadron transition form factors $G_M^*$, $G_E^*$, and $G_C^*$. AICc model selection yields a modified dipole for $G_M^*$, a dipole for $G_E^*$, and a cubic $z$ expansion for $G_C^*$. These fits define the imposed positive-$x$ normalization $F_α(t)=2G_α^*(-t)$ for factorized, correlated exponential, Regge-like, and double-distribution-inspired transition-GPD profiles. The upper boundary of the impact-parameter transform is fixed by the largest measured absolute-form-factor point, $Q^2=6~\mathrm{GeV}^2$, so that no high-$Q^2$ continuation beyond the measured range enters the production reconstruction. The primary transverse localization observable is therefore defined from the small-$Q^2$ slope of the modeled transition GPD, with finite-window radial moments retained only as secondary core-shape diagnostics. For the slope-defined width, the transition form factor contributes an $x$-independent channel-dependent offset, while the entire $x$ dependence is fixed by the chosen longitudinal--transverse profile ansatz. The factorized profile is $x$-independent and the three non-factorized families generate distinct modeled $x$ dependences. The resulting reconstruction separates measured transition-form-factor information from model-dependent longitudinal structure and provides a controlled framework for assessing structural and covariance sensitivity in $N\toΔ(1232)$ transition tomography.

title: Generalized transverse-momentum-dependent parton distributions of a photon and orbital angular momentum
abstract: The coefficients of generalized transverse-momentum-dependent distributions (GTMDs) that encode the canonical fermion orbital angular momentum and spin--orbit correlation do not contribute to the direct transverse-momentum-dependent (TMD) and generalized-parton-distribution (GPD) projections. We present, to our knowledge, the first explicit calculation of the leading-twist, time-even, chiral-even fermion GTMDs of an on-shell real photon at zero skewness and order $α$. The coefficients $\mathcal{F}_A$ and $\mathcal{G}_A$, which multiply the $k_\perp\timesΔ_\perp$ structure, yield the fermion orbital angular momentum $\ell_z^f$ and spin--orbit correlation $\mathcal{C}_z^f$. For photon helicity $+1$, both are obtained in closed form in the leading fermion--antifermion sector and obey $\mathcal{C}_z^f=-\ell_z^f/2$ for a common transverse regulator independent of $x$, because the channel with the active fermion's spin anti-aligned with its orbital motion carries three times the integrated weight of the aligned channel. The projections reproduce the known photon TMDs and leading-logarithmic photon-to-fermion kernels, and energy-momentum-tensor overlaps reproduce the known one-loop photon gravitational form factors $F_1$, $F_2$, and $F_3$. Our result provides an analytic benchmark for fermionic orbital and spin--orbit structure in the real photon.

title: On reflection positivity of lattice chiral fermions
abstract: We point out that the overlap Weyl fermion, the spacetime lattice realization of a Weyl fermion underlying Lüscher's construction of lattice chiral gauge theories, is not reflection positive in two and four dimensions at finite lattice spacing. Consequently, the standard Osterwalder--Schrader reconstruction does not yield a Hilbert space with a self-adjoint Hamiltonian. In two dimensions, we further show that the overlap Weyl fermion cannot be cut open: the lattice action becomes nonlocal in the presence of a boundary, as expected from the gravitational anomaly of the continuum field theory. By contrast, the overlap Dirac fermion is known to be reflection positive. However, its compact axial symmetry is not invariant under the reflection, whereas a reflection-invariant axial symmetry is noncompact, and both are part of an Onsager algebra.

title: Thermal deep inelastic scattering, universality and complex geodesics
abstract: In deep inelastic scattering (DIS), a lepton scatters off a target hadron whose structure is probed by an exchanged photon with large spacelike virtuality. We consider two-point functions of currents in strongly interacting quantum field theories at finite temperature in this kinematic regime and use a holographic description to compute them. At large virtuality, the crossover from vacuum-dominated to thermally dominated physics corresponds to a transition from exponentially suppressed absorption to power-law behavior of the response functions. This regime is related to a particular near-lightcone limit of thermal CFT correlators. We show that the response functions exhibit a large degree of universality: the dependence on the three-point couplings of currents to the stress tensor enters through a channel-dependent coefficient multiplying the kinematic parameter that controls the relative size of vacuum and thermal effects. The same coefficient controls conformal collider bounds; when either bound is saturated, the corresponding response function takes its vacuum form in the near-lightcone limit. Furthermore, the absorption exponent in the low-temperature regime is related to a complex geodesic propagating in the near-lightcone geometry.

title: Spatiotemporal K-Shape: Reconstructing inhomogeneous condensate profiles on the lattice
abstract: Spatially modulated chiral condensates can affect the phase structure of dense QCD effective models. Understanding such order requires characterizing its real-space structure as well as detecting a modulation. Spatial two-point correlators retain the ensemble-averaged power spectrum but discard relative Fourier phases, leaving the configuration shapes undetermined in general. We propose the Spatiotemporal K-Shape method to extract representative shapes from lattice Monte Carlo ensembles without assuming a functional form. The method extends K-Shape clustering to periodic lattice fields, aligning configurations modulo translations and, optionally, a global sign or phase before extracting cluster centroids. Comparisons across clusterings assess whether one representative shape suffices. Controlled tests recover distinct profiles with identical correlators and separate mixtures of different shapes. Applied to the $(1+1)$-dimensional Gross-Neveu model with $N_f=8$, the method extracts non-sinusoidal profiles with two sign changes at two chemical potentials and separates multiple shape families at a third, where a single centroid is insufficient. Including the discrete chiral sign symmetry in the alignment can fold domain-length fluctuations into an asymmetric centroid without implying a preferred ensemble asymmetry. The method thus complements correlator diagnostics with representative real-space shapes and information on their diversity. The application to the Gross-Neveu model provides a testing ground for configuration-based studies of inhomogeneous order relevant to the QCD phase diagram.

title: Electromagnetic cross section of charmonium decay
abstract: As an important measurable quantity, the electromagnetic cross sections of charmonium decay in an e+e- collider are valuated for fifteen final states. A general scheme of lS-coupling analysis is adopted for constructing covariant helicity-coupling amplitudes involving two-body decays with arbitrary integer spins. Based on the decay rate, the collision cross section is obtained finally. A number of illustrative examples is worked out to expound and incarnate the general formulas.
